title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (R)
text:
Dataset Overview
The Gapminder dataset provides country-level records over 5-year intervals from 1952 to 2007.

library(gapminder)
library(dplyr)

glimpse(gapminder)

Rows: 1,704
Columns: 6

$ continent <fct> Asia, Asia, Asia, Asia, Asia, Asia, Asia, Asia, Asia, Asia, …
$ year      <int> 1952, 1957, 1962, 1967, 1972, 1977, 1982, 1987, 1992, 1997, …
$ lifeExp   <dbl> 28.801, 30.332, 31.997, 34.020, 36.088, 38.438, 39.854, 40.8…
$ pop       <int> 8425333, 9240934, 10267083, 11537966, 13079460, 14880372, 12…

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (R)
text:
Continental Overview in 2007

summary_2007 <- gapminder |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(
    median_life_exp = median(lifeExp),
    median_gdp = median(gdpPercap),
    total_population = sum(as.numeric(pop)),
    num_countries = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(median_life_exp))

knitr::kable(summary_2007, digits = 2, caption = "2007 Continental Summary")

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (R)
text:
Longitudinal Life Expectancy Trajectory


Code
yearly_trend <- gapminder |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(median_life_exp = median(lifeExp))

plot(
  yearly_trend$year,
  yearly_trend$median_life_exp,
  type = "b",
  pch = 19,
  col = "navy",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Median Life Expectancy (Years)",
  main = "Global Median Life Expectancy (1952 - 2007)"
)
grid()








Figure 1: Global median life expectancy progression from 1952 to 2007.






Visualizing Continental Life Expectancy (2007)


Code
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(summary_2007, aes(x = continent, y = median_life_exp, fill = continent)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(
    title = "Median Life Expectancy by Continent (2007)",
    x = "Continent",
    y = "Median Life Expectancy (years)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (Python)
text:
Regional Summary (2007)
Comparing median life expectancy and GDP per capita across continents in the most recent survey year:

recent_summary = (
    gapminder[gapminder["year"] == 2007]
    .groupby("continent")
    .agg(
        median_life_exp=("lifeExp", "median"),
        median_gdp=("gdpPercap", "median"),
        total_pop=("pop", "sum"),
        country_count=("country", "count")
    )
    .sort_values(by="median_life_exp", ascending=False)
    .reset_index()
)

title: Global Life Expectancy Trends (Python)
text:
55-Year Progress (1952 vs 2007)


Code
comparison = (
    gapminder[gapminder["year"].isin([1952, 2007])]
    .groupby(["continent", "year"])["lifeExp"]
    .mean()
    .unstack()
    .rename(columns={1952: "life_exp_1952", 2007: "life_exp_2007"})
)

comparison["gain_years"] = comparison["life_exp_2007"] - comparison["life_exp_1952"]
comparison.round(2)

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
Orientation day on campus.


MDS moves fast. Orientation week was hectic, but super fun at the same time. I did ask myself “What did I get myself into quite a few times” but week one made me realise I was exactly where I’m supposed to be.
Making friends was easy, Cohort 11 has some super cool people. I was fascinated to learn that MDS this year has students from 35+ nationalities. I dont think I have ever been in a room with such diversity.
Coming out of a whirlwind of team-building exercises, technical workshops, and wellness sessions, both the cohort and I are fully primed to tackle the challenges ahead!

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
By default, R might try to use your system’s global Python. To ensure true reproducibility, we explicitly tell the reticulate package to use the Python binary inside our uv virtual environment.

library(reticulate)

# Force reticulate to use the project's .venv
use_virtualenv("../../.venv", required = TRUE)

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
Creating Data in R
First, let’s create a simple dataframe using R.

# Create a small dataset in R
r_data <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  score = c(85, 92, 78, 90, 88)
)
print(r_data)

  id score
1  1    85
2  2    92
3  3    78
4  4    90
5  5    88

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
text:
Reading R Data into Python
Now, we switch to a Python chunk. We can read the R object natively into Python by calling r.name (where “name” is the variable we created in R).

import pandas as pd

# Access the R dataframe using r.r_data
python_df = r.r_data

# Modify the dataframe using Python (adding a curve to the score)
python_df['curved_score'] = python_df['score'] + 5
print(python_df)

   id  score  curved_score
0   1   85.0          90.0
1   2   92.0          97.0
2   3   78.0          83.0
3   4   90.0          95.0
4   5   88.0          93.0

title: Python and R Interoperability Bonus
section: Returning Python Data back to R
text:
Returning Python Data back to R
Finally, we switch back to an R chunk. We can retrieve the modified dataframe from Python by calling py$name.

# Access the modified Python dataframe using py$python_df
final_r_data <- py$python_df

# Display the curved scores back in R
print(final_r_data)

  id score curved_score
1  1    85           90
2  2    92           97
3  3    78           83
4  4    90           95
5  5    88           93
